Former Virginia Republican Rep. Barbara Comstock poured cold water on the GOP's prospects for the 2026 midterms Sunday, citing what she said was an especially grim remark from a Republican strategist.

On an MSNBC panel discussion on "The Weekend," Comstock weighed in on two recent reports about Republicans' midterm prospects — one from Axios revealing that a Senate Republican pollster delivered rosy predictions at a closed-door GOP meeting only to be told he was "smoking something"; and one reporting that, amid concerns Republicans could face wipeout losses in which even traditionally safe seats could be at risk, Donald Trump was instead heading to deep-red Alabama in October for a rally.

"I think the election was decided in the summer, and it's late September now," said Comstock, who left Congress in 2019. "Donald Trump has spent the entire summer trying to lose for Republicans." She pointed to his unpopular war in Iran causing gas prices to rise and interest rates to spike.

Comstock recalled a comment from an anonymous Republican strategist that came after Senate Majority Leader John Thune hit the trail in Georgia with GOP Senate candidate Mike Collins; she noted that Collins was "double digits behind" Democratic incumbent Sen. Jon Ossoff in polling.

The strategist said, per Comstock: "We're just trying to make the patient comfortable now." She suggested Trump's planned Alabama rally reflected the same mindset.

"I think sending Donald Trump to Alabama is to make the patient comfortable," she added.

Democratic strategist Ameshia Cross quipped in response: "America itself is on life support, so I don't know how much more comfortable they can make the patient."
